items.followUp: Give an example of an incorrect data format when entering a date.

rubric.why: Shows understanding that a wrong data format does not follow the required format.
rubric.description: Explain what makes a data format wrong.
rubric.how: State that the entered data does not match the required format or type.

rubric.why: Gives a specific example of a data-format error.
rubric.description: Give an example of a wrong data format.
rubric.how: For example, entering letters in a field that requires a number.

modelAnswer: A wrong data format occurs when data is entered in a format that does not match the required format.
For example, entering “ABC” in a field that requires a person’s age in numbers is a wrong data format.

items.followUp: Define volatile memory and give one example.

rubric.why: States the key property of non-volatile memory.
rubric.how: Explain that it retains stored data when the power is off.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of non-volatile memory.
rubric.how: Name ROM or another non-volatile storage device.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is switched off.
An example is Read Only Memory (ROM).

items.followUp: What are the two possible truth values of a Boolean variable?

rubric.why: Identifies the other possible truth value.

modelAnswer: Truth values are the two values used to represent the result of a logical expression.
They are True and False (often represented by 1 and 0, respectively).

items.followUp: What is phishing, and how can a user avoid it?

rubric.why: Captures the defining feature of hacking.
rubric.how: Describe gaining access to a computer or network without authorization.

rubric.description: State what may be accessed or attacked.
rubric.how: Mention a computer, network, or its data.

modelAnswer: Hacking is gaining unauthorized access to a computer, network or its data.
It may be done to view, steal, change or damage information.

items.followUp: Describe one advantage and one disadvantage of bus topology.

rubric.why: Identifies the shared backbone cable used in bus topology.
rubric.how: State that all devices connect to a single main cable.

rubric.why: Includes a characteristic arrangement of the bus cable.
rubric.how: Mention that terminators are fitted at both ends of the cable.

modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all computers and other devices are connected to one main cable called the bus or backbone.
Terminators are placed at both ends of the cable.
